findings.reason: a coordinator reading "all met" dispatches a 618–1,226-name generation run whose whole stated justification is that the source-loss generators are shut, while two of them are still unbuilt.
findings.text: §50 states "The source-loss generators are closed: §45–§48. All are met before launch", but the same document declares s45 and s46 `implementable` (plan.html:276, plan.html:280), so two of the four generator sections it names as closed are open, and the lead's own launch condition ("iff the pipeline is a stable state") is therefore not established by the section's own record

findings.reason: an undeclared dependency cannot hold a launch, so the precondition exists only as prose that a dispatch need not read, which is the same defect as a gate that never runs.
findings.text: §50's section element carries `data-links=""`, so the four work-backlog sections its prose names as preconditions (and the schema-registration the task depends on) are declared nowhere in the section's relationships; nothing in the plan orders `sib-full-dd-run` behind §45–§49

findings.reason: the pin is one of the four preconditions the section declares met, and a run launched on it would record 1.13 as the answering build for every call, which is exactly the property the `openai-model-refresh-code` dependency was meant to guarantee.
findings.text: the precondition "Jev seats are pinned to `typesafe/jev-1.14`, with the answering build recorded per call (`openai-model-refresh-code`)" does not hold in the tree: `pyproject.toml:381,450,457,466` and `imas_codex/settings.py:189,193,197,229` all read `typesafe/jev-1.13`, and no `jev-1.14` appears anywhere under `imas_codex/`, `pyproject.toml` or `agents/`

findings.reason: the reprice to USD 80–160 rests on discounting the estimate's USD 664 as a panel-pricing artefact, whereas the cited review found part of that gap is an arithmetic defect in the estimate's own spend model, so the plan argues past its data on the one number that leads to the cap.
findings.text: §50 cites the estimate as "`sib-dd-completion-estimate` (merge `53d6106c3`, reviews 82 and 82)", but the plan's own record of that run carries two reviews, the first scoring 82 (17+17+20+8+15+5) and the second 69 (10+14+20+6+14+5), and the second is the one that found a blocking defect: "spend() multiplies the phase call count by the sum of each configured seat's per-call cost, overstating review_name and review_docs roughly 3-4x and the USD 664 headline about 2.4x" (plan.html:1057-1063), so §50 presents a reviewed-with-a-blocking-finding estimate as twice-scored-at-82 and then attributes the entire gap to the retired paid panel

findings.reason: a full DD run that starts, errors inside the first phase, and exits without exceeding the cap satisfies every bullet but the first, so the section's gate cannot distinguish a composition of 1,000 names from a run that composed none.
findings.text: §50's done-when measures that "the run finishes or stops at its cap" and that "the live read-back gives names created by stage", with no floor on names created against the 618–1,226 yield the section itself states, no base arm, and no negative control; and its fourth bullet ("the export gate's blocking set is still 0") is true on the unrun tree and so measures nothing; a run that finished having created no name passes every bullet the section sets
